documents.title: Liver Transplant Discharge Summary
documents.author: transplant surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL LIVER TRANSPLANT CENTER
Admitted: 09/19/2022  Discharged: 09/30/2022
Indication: decompensated cirrhosis from chronic hepatitis C (genotype 1a) and prior alcohol use, with hepatocellular carcinoma treated by partial right hepatectomy in January 2022.
Procedure 09/19: orthotopic deceased-donor liver transplantation. Uneventful anastomoses. Extubated postoperative day 1.
Course: graft function improved steadily with falling bilirubin and INR. Graft ultrasound on day 1 and day 5 showed patent vessels. Ascites resolved; diuretics stopped. Transferred from the ICU on day 3. Tacrolimus titrated to target trough.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Discharge medications:
- tacrolimus 2 mg by mouth twice daily
- mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg by mouth twice daily
- prednisone 5 mg by mouth daily
- trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg by mouth daily (Pneumocystis prophylaxis)
- calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
Stopped: spironolactone, furosemide.
Follow-up: transplant clinic twice weekly for the first month with labs, including tacrolimus troughs; then tapering visits. PCP within 2 to 3 weeks. No live vaccines. Inactivated influenza vaccine may be given after the first month.

documents.title: Post-Transplant Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
57M, 3.5 weeks after deceased-donor liver transplant (9/19). Discharge summary reviewed.
S: Feels better than he has in two years, still tires by mid-afternoon. Eating well. Incision healing; seen by transplant clinic twice a week, labs Mon/Thu. Taking tacrolimus 2 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX DS daily. Uses a pill box and phone alarms. No fevers, no diarrhea.
O: vitals as charted. No icterus. Chevron incision clean and dry, no erythema. Abdomen soft, no fluid wave. No edema.
A/P:
1. Liver transplant status: immunosuppression per transplant center. Problem list updated: cirrhosis, portal hypertension and low platelets resolved with the new liver; HCC moved to history. Platelets normal today.
2. Chronic hepatitis C: remains on the list.
3. Labs today as a courtesy for transplant clinic, results faxed there.
4. Vaccines: inactivated flu and updated COVID in November once past the first month. No live vaccines ever going forward, reviewed.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPT
Visit 12/03/2022, arrived 16:45 by private car.
CC: abdominal pain, sudden, 2 hours.
HPI: 57-year-old man about 10 weeks after liver transplant. Abrupt severe pain across the whole abdomen that started while watching TV and has not let up; nothing makes it better or worse. For about a week, burning in the pit of the stomach after eating, which he treated with over-the-counter antacids now and then; did not call anyone. Takes prednisone and other transplant medicines. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals: T 38.2 C, BP 96/60, HR 112.
Exam: lying very still, sweaty. Abdomen distended, tender everywhere with guarding and marked rebound. No bowel sounds.
Upright CXR: free air under the diaphragm.
Impression: perforated viscus, likely peptic, in an immunosuppressed patient. Fluids, IV antibiotics, IV PPI. Transplant team and general surgery at bedside; to the OR.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Date of operation: 12/03/2022
Preoperative diagnosis: pneumoperitoneum. Postoperative diagnosis: perforated anterior duodenal ulcer.
Procedure: exploratory laparotomy, omental (Graham) patch repair of perforated duodenal ulcer, washout.
Findings: a small perforation of the anterior wall of the first part of the duodenum with bilious contamination of the upper abdomen. Liver graft appeared healthy. No other perforation.
The omental pedicle was secured over the defect with interrupted sutures; leak test negative. Abdomen irrigated. Fascia closed. EBL minimal. Patient to the surgical ICU in stable condition.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admitted: 12/03/2022  Discharged: 12/10/2022
Diagnosis: perforated duodenal ulcer, s/p Graham patch repair 12/03. Background: liver transplant 09/2022 on tacrolimus, mycophenolate, prednisone.
Course: one night in the surgical ICU, then the floor. IV antibiotics completed. Diet advanced from day 4. Tacrolimus continued with levels checked by the transplant team throughout. Wound healing well.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily for 8 weeks (new); tacrolimus 2 mg twice daily; mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily; prednisone 5 mg daily; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS daily.
Instructions: avoid NSAIDs. Surgical clinic 2 weeks. PCP 1 to 2 weeks.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up: perforated duodenal ulcer 12/3, Graham patch the same night. ED, op note and discharge summary reviewed.
S: Sore along the new midline wound, otherwise ok. Eating small meals without burning. Taking pantoprazole 40 BID. Transplant meds unchanged, levels per transplant clinic. Says he should have called about the burning that week, assumed it was his usual heartburn.
O: afebrile, vitals as charted. Midline incision clean, edges together, no drainage. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near the wound.
A/P:
- Perforated DU s/p repair: pantoprazole 40 BID for 8 weeks total (to early Feb), then stop and reassess. No NSAIDs, ever; this is on his list. Low threshold to call for epigastric pain given prednisone.
- Liver transplant: stable.
- CBC today.
RTC early Feb.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 8 weeks of pantoprazole done this week. No epigastric pain, no black stools. Heartburn only now and then, uses calcium carbonate. Back in the shop part time, light work. Weight coming back.
O: vitals as charted. Midline scar well healed, no hernia felt. Abdomen soft, nontender.
A/P:
- Perforated DU, repaired: course complete, pantoprazole stopped. Resolved. PRN calcium carbonate for heartburn.
- Liver transplant: transplant clinic monthly now. CMP/CBC today, copy to them.
- Hep C: on list.
Physical in the fall.

REGIONAL LIVER TRANSPLANT CENTER, POST-TRANSPLANT CLINIC
Visit 04/12/2023
Mr. Nowak is now about 7 months after liver transplantation. He recovered from the December ulcer repair without problems. Graft function is stable and tacrolimus troughs have been in our target range on 2 mg twice daily. We are continuing mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily, prednisone 5 mg daily and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Next visit in 4 months with labs. Thank you for sharing his care.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
58M, a year out from liver transplant.
How he's doing: working close to full days again on a lighter schedule. Energy good. No heartburn to speak of. Sober 7 years.
Meds: tacrolimus 2 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, TMP-SMX DS daily, calcium carbonate PRN. NKDA.
Functional: independent in all ADLs/IADLs. No falls. Hearing and vision ok.
Prevention: colonoscopy 9/2021 normal (10 yr). Hep A/B, zoster, PCV20, Tdap complete. Flu/COVID next month at a nurse visit. Glucose and A1c checked given prednisone and family history: A1c 5.6.
Exam: well. Anicteric. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen: well-healed chevron and midline scars, no hernia, no tenderness. Skin: no suspicious lesions on a full check. No edema.
A/P: stable post-transplant. Labs as above, copy to transplant clinic. Sun protection reviewed given immunosuppression and outdoor work.
